source.text: Τί, φημί, ὑπήνεγκαν; Ἄκουε, φησίν· μάστιγας, φυλακάς, θλίψεις μεγάλας, σταυρούς, θηρία εἵνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματος· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκείνων ἐστὶν τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ ἁγιάσματος, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν πάθῃ διὰ τὸ ὄνομα· τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν τὰ ἀριστερὰ μέρη ἐστίν. ἀλλὰ ἀμφοτέρων, καὶ τῶν ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ τῶν ἐξ ἀριστερῶν καθημένων, τὰ αὐτὰ δῶρα καὶ αἱ αὐταὶ ἐπαγγελίαι· μόνον ἐκεῖνοι ἐκ δεξιῶν κάθηνται καὶ ἔχουσιν δόξαν τινά. 2. σὺ δὲ κατεπίθυμος εἰ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μετ’ αὐτῶν, ἀλλὰ τὰ ὑστερήματά σου πολλὰ· καθαρισθήσῃ δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ὑστερημάτων σου καὶ πάντες δὲ οἱ μὴ διψυχοῦντες καθαρισθήσονται ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων εἰς ταύτην τὴν ἡμέραν. 3. ταῦτα εἴπασα ἤθελεν ἀπελθεῖν· πεσὼν δὲ αὐτῆς πρὸς τοὺς πόδας ἠρώτησα αὐτὴν κατὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἵνα μοι ἐπιδείξῃ ὃ ἐπηγγείλατο ὅραμα. 4. ἡ δὲ πάλιν ἐπελάβετό μου τῆς χειρὸς καὶ ἐγείρει με καὶ καθίζει ἐπὶ τὸ συμπλέσιον ἐξ εὐωνύμων· ἐκαθέζετο δὲ καὶ αὐτὴ ἐκ δεξιῶν. καὶ ἐπάρασα ῥάβδον τινα λαμπρὰν λέγει μοι· Βλέπεις μέγα πρᾶγμα; λέγω αὐτῇ· Κυρία, οὐδὲν βλέπω. λέγει μοι· [Σὺ,] ἰδοὺ οὐχ ὁρᾷς κατέναντί σου πύργον μέγαν οἰκοδομούμενον ἐπὶ ὑδάτων λίθοις τετραγώνοις λαμπροῖς; 5. ἐν τετραγώνῳ δὲ ᾠκοδομεῖτο ὁ πύργος ὑπὸ τῶν ἓξ νεανίσκων τῶν ἐληλυθότων μετ’ αὐτῆς· ἄλλαι δὲ μυριάδες ἀνδρῶν παρεφέρον λίθους, οἱ μὲν ἐκ τοῦ βυθοῦ, οἱ δὲ ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐπεδίδουν τοῖς ἓξ νεανίσκοις. ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἐλάμβανον καὶ ᾠκοδόμουν· 6. τοὺς μὲν ἐκ τοῦ βυθοῦ λίθους ἑλκομένους πάντας οὕτως ἐτίθεσαν εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν· ἡρμοσμένοι γὰρ ἦσαν καὶ συνεφώνουν τῇ ἁρμογῇ μετὰ τῶν ἑτέρων λίθων· καὶ οὕτως ἐκολλῶντο ἀλλήλοις, ὥστε τὴν ἁρμογὴν αὐτῶν μὴ φαίνεσθαι. ἐφαίνετο δὲ ἡ οἰκοδομὴ τοῦ πύργου ὡς ἐξ ἑνὸς λίθου ᾠκοδομημένη. 7. τοὺς δὲ ἑτέρους λίθους τοὺς φερομένους ἀπὸ τῆς ξηρᾶς τοὺς μὲν ἀπέβαλλον, τοὺς δὲ ἐτίθουν εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν· ἄλλους δὲ κατέκοπτον καὶ ἔρριπτον μακρὰν ἀπὸ τοῦ πύργου. 8. ἄλλοι δὲ λίθοι πολλοὶ κύκλῳ τοῦ πύργου ἔκειντο, καὶ οὐκ ἐχρῶντο αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν· ἦσαν γάρ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐψωριακότες, ἕτεροι δὲ σχισμὰς ἔχοντες, ἄλλοι δὲ κεκολοβωμένοι, ἄλλοι δὲ λευκοὶ καὶ στρογγύλοι, μὴ ἁρμόζοντες εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν. 9. ἔβλεπον δὲ ἑτέρους λίθους ῥιπτομένους μακρὰν ἀπὸ τοῦ πύργου καὶ ἐρχομένους εἰς τὴν ὁδὸν καὶ μὴ μένοντας ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἀλλὰ κυλιομένους εἰς τὴν ἀνοδίαν· ἑτέρους δὲ ἐπὶ πῦρ ἐμπίπτοντας καὶ καιομένους· ἑτέρους δὲ πίπτοντας ἐγγὺς ὑδάτων καὶ μὴ δυναμένους κυλισθῆναι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ, καίπερ θελόντων κυλισθῆναι καὶ ἐλθεῖν εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.

translation.text:
1[1]. “What,” I said, “did they endure?” She says, “Listen: scourges, prisons, great afflictions[2], crucifixions, wild beasts—for the sake of the Name. For this reason the right-hand parts of the sanctuary belong to them, and to whoever suffers because of the Name; but the left-hand parts belong to the rest. Yet for both, those sitting on the right and those on the left, the gifts are the same and the promises the same—only those on the right sit there and have some glory.”

2. “But you are very eager to sit on the right with them; yet your shortcomings are many. Still, you will be cleansed from your shortcomings, and all who are not double-minded will be cleansed from all their sins up to this day.”

3. After she had said these things, she wanted to depart; but I fell at her feet and asked her by the Lord to show me the vision that she had promised me.

4. And again she took hold of my hand, raised me up, and seated me on the plaited bench on the left; and she herself sat on the right. And, lifting up a certain bright rod, she says to me, “Do you see a great thing?” I say to her, “Lady, I see nothing.” She says to me, “[You,] look—do you not see opposite you a great tower being built upon the waters with square-cut, shining stones?”

5. The tower was being built foursquare by the six young men who had come with her; and myriads of other men were bringing stones, some from the deep and others from the land, and were handing them to the six young men. They would take them and build.

6. The stones hauled up from the deep they set, every one, into the building just as they were; for they were fitted and matched the jointing with the other stones, and so were cemented to one another, so that their joint was not visible. The construction of the tower appeared as if it had been built from a single stone.

7. But of the other stones being brought from the dry land, some they were rejecting, and some they were putting into the building; others they were cutting and throwing far from the tower.

8. Many other stones lay around the tower, and they were not using them for the building—for some of them were scabby, others had cracks, others had been truncated, others were white and round, not fitting for the building.

9. And I saw other stones being hurled far from the tower and coming into the road, and not remaining in the road but rolling into the trackless places; others falling onto a fire and being burned; others falling near waters and not being able to roll into the water[13][12][11][10][9][8][7][6][5][4][3], though they wanted to roll and come into the water.

footnotes.text: “Crucifixions” translates σταυρούς; some prefer “crosses” as metonymy for the punishment.
“Because of the Name” is early Christian idiom for suffering on account of Jesus’ name; the Greek leaves the referent implicit.
“Sanctuary” renders ἁγίασμα; alternatives include “holy place” or “sacred precinct.”
“Not double‑minded” translates μὴ διψυχοῦντες; alternatives include “not wavering.” The term is a stock vice in Hermas.
“Up to this day” (εἰς ταύτην τὴν ἡμέραν) can also be read “as of this day.”
“Plaited bench” (συμπλέσιον) refers to seating made of interlaced material (e.g., twigs or rushes).
Some witnesses include an emphatic “You,” here: “[You,] look …”.
“Foursquare” renders ἐν τετραγώνῳ; it may also be translated “in a square.”
“Myriads” (μυριάδες) literally means tens of thousands; here it conveys an immense number.
“Trackless places” translates ἀνοδία (lit. ‘no‑road’); also possible: “pathless places.”
Wild beasts (θηρία) evokes execution by animals in Roman arenas.

Alludes to arena execution by beasts; “wild beasts” is the idiomatic phrase.
Early Christian idiom for allegiance to Jesus; capitalizing preserves the reverential idiom without forcing a specific expansion.
“Side” fits spatial imagery of a sanctuary with seating; keeps symmetry with right/left motif.
“Sanctuary” renders the sacred-space nuance and maintains temple imagery without over‑specifying.
Here contrasts status with equal divine bestowals; “gifts” better than “rewards,” which could skew to merit.
Standard rendering; communicates divine assurances without legalistic overtones.
Keeps doxa as ‘glory’ while acknowledging an undefined measure with ‘some’.
Conveys strong desire in accessible English.
Moral‑spiritual lacks; “shortcomings” is idiomatic and non‑technical.
Cleansing imagery is consistent with Hermas’ penitential theology; passive voice retained.
Hermas regularly attacks ‘double‑mindedness’; this preserves that stock vice term (cf. Jas 1:8).
Baseline moral category; avoids euphemism.
Retains material image of interlaced seating; ‘bench’ fits the seating scene.
“Rod” matches common prophetic/visionary implements; ‘bright’ renders λαμπρά.
Core symbol in Hermas; literal rendering preserved.
Preposition ἐπί with genitive conveys location ‘upon’; literal phrasing retains symbolic force.
“Square‑cut” fits stones; “foursquare” preserves traditional architectural idiom for the tower.
Neutral, natural English; avoids modern connotations of ‘youths’.
Literal and evocative; preserves numerical hyperbole of the scene.
Aquatic depth without over‑specifying a sea‑bed.
Contrasts with ‘the deep’; ‘land’ fits the parallelism.
Maintains building‑trade vocabulary; ‘jointing’ expresses the join as a system.
Concrete image of bonding masonry; ‘cemented’ fits stonework better than ‘glued’.
Standard collocation; balances with ‘deep’.
Captures evaluative and physical action implied by context.
Stone‑shaping action; kept general to avoid over‑specifying technique.
Psōra denotes scab/mange; ‘scabby’ conveys defilement imagery.
Plain description of flawed stones.
Stone metaphor favors ‘truncated/cut short’ over bodily ‘maimed’.
Literal; suggests aesthetic yet unsuitable stones.
Continues the building‑fit motif.
More vivid for violent casting away.
Contrasts with ‘trackless’ (no‑road); ‘road’ best preserves play on ὁδός/ἀνοδία.
Alpha‑privative formation (‘no road’) preserved in English idiom.
Prepositional nuance (ἐπί) retained; both convey peril.

theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas uses early Christian idiom where ‘the Name’ signifies allegiance to Jesus. Leaving it unexpanded preserves the idiom and its reverential tone while not foreclosing whether ‘Lord’ or ‘Jesus’ is in view.

theological_decisions.issue: Right‑ and left‑hand sides in the sanctuary
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Equal gifts and promises; right‑hand seating conveys honor for suffering
alternative_readings: Right side implies higher salvation status
theological_decisions.rationale: The text explicitly states the gifts and promises are the same for both sides; only a ‘some glory’ distinction is noted for those who suffered for the Name.

theological_decisions.issue: Cleansing “up to this day” and non‑double‑mindedness
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Temporal extent refers to the present day of the vision and the possibility of cleansing for those not double‑minded
alternative_readings: A special eschatological ‘day’ of repentance only
‘On this day’ as a liturgical fast day
theological_decisions.rationale: The phrase εἰς ταύτην τὴν ἡμέραν most naturally reads as a terminus ad quem (‘up to this day’) in narrative time; Hermas elsewhere links cleansing with single‑hearted repentance.
Given the martyr list (scourges, prisons, beasts), the punishment itself is meant; ‘crucifixions’ foregrounds the suffering endured.
Maintains sacred‑space imagery without prescribing Temple architecture; fits Hermas’ visionary cultic symbolism.
Hermas develops ‘double‑mindedness’ as a stock vice beyond mere doubt; keeping the term preserves continuity with his paraenesis.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Literal rendering without interpretive expansion (e.g., baptism)
theological_decisions.rationale: The vision will itself interpret symbols later; translation should not pre‑empt Hermas’ own exegesis.

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate, preserving the vocabulary, tone, and symbolic force of Hermas exceptionally well. A minor adjustment is suggested in verse 7 to maintain the continuous aspect of the imperfect verbs describing the ongoing sorting and building process.
issues_found: In verse 7, the imperfect verb ἐτίθουν is translated as the simple past 'put', which slightly flattens the continuous aspect established by the surrounding imperfects ('kept rejecting', 'were cutting'). Changing to 'were putting' restores the ongoing nature of the action and maintains consistency.

revisions.rationale: Improved lexical accuracy and formality: changed several renderings to better match the Greek (e.g., “imprisonments” for φυλακάς, “crosses” for σταυρούς, “for the sake of the Name,” “parts” for μέρη, “asked” for ἠρώτησα, “bench” for συμπλέσιον, “square” for τετραγώνοις/ἐν τετραγώνῳ, “bringing/handing” for imperfects, “joined” instead of “cemented,” “mutilated” for κεκολοβωμένοι, and “wasteland” for ἀνοδίαν). Also smoothed a few English phrases for naturalness and consistency.

translation.text: 1. “What,” I said, “did they endure?” She says, “Listen: scourges, imprisonments, great afflictions, crosses, wild beasts—for the sake of the Name. For this reason the right-hand parts of the sanctuary belong to them, and to whoever suffers because of the Name; but the left-hand parts belong to the rest. Yet for both, those sitting on the right and those on the left, the gifts are the same and the promises the same—only those on the right sit there and have some glory.”
